value: CC, from Akien's TOOLS idea of 2026-08-11

node_classes/_charter+why.json says a record defines 'its invariant and its VARIABLE GATE-SET', and 'a pipeline is just the gate-set on a node-class'. Every registered class names a distinct prove_gate: code-seam = the tester runs the proof; concept-piece = a quorum of reviewers; host-seam = measure the HOST plus REBUILD plus an expiring RE-VERIFY; skill = the cairnmap derivation gate; operational-driver = proof plus method-registry plus owned-target. 'device' names NO gate-set — a device is proved by exercising its code, which IS code-seam. So the missing thing is a SECOND AXIS, not a node_class and not a folder. The registry's charter is not violated by this ticket; it is what RULES device out of the class registry.

Is tool-ness a property of the COMPONENT or of the RELATIONSHIP? import_sieve classed itself 'primitive (a library, not a device)' and is a library to its callers while being a gate at the ruling door. If the kind depends on who holds it, one field per component cannot carry it and a tools/ FOLDER would be actively wrong. This is the assumption the build tests FIRST — it decides the shape of everything after it.

WHERE the field lives (a charter-schema key or a second registry beside node_classes/) and what it is CALLED under build-to-the-tool naming — the term must be derivable from its native-domain use, not memorized.

Is node_class required or optional? Twelve lab charters carry none, eleven of them skills, while 'skill' IS a registered class. Either the field is required and 12 charters are red, or it binds only at cast — different rules, and only one can be true.
members_so_far is stale registry-wide and no door writes it. Law 6 asks who owns that write; the honest candidates are derive-it-from-the-charters or delete the field.

Does Akien's word TOOLS mean this axis? He named a felt gap; the reshape is CC's reading of it. A class or axis DEFINITION is ratified at his signature gate, so this routes to him and is not settled by the build.

the charter schema — record the distinction: node_class answers 'how is this PROVED', the new axis answers 'what does this ACT AS at runtime'. A compound string like 'code-seam (a spine device by role...)' becomes two fields instead of one overloaded one.

Of the five registered node classes, only code-seam and skill have workflow_versions registered. concept-piece, host-seam and operational-driver have NONE — so casting any node as one of those three would be REFUSED by the emit chokepoint at its first crossing. Three of five registered classes are uncastable today, and nothing announces it until a voyage dies. THIS TICKET HAD TO CAST ITSELF AS code-seam FOR EXACTLY THAT REASON: it is arguably a concept-piece by content, and that class cannot carry a node. The registry's own gap forced the classification — the incoherence this ticket exists to fix, demonstrating itself at the cast.
device-ness-is-decided-at-the-shim — defines what the value 'device' MEANS on the new axis. Recorded ruling order: base-device first, then THIS ticket, then alarms.

value.it_bit: Before the firing this ticket said 'device is not a class, it is a second axis' and stopped there — which would have carried inheritance-membership forward untouched and re-created the defect one field to the left. The probe separated the CONCEPT from its MEMBERSHIP RULE, which is what makes the sibling ticket device-ness-is-decided-at-the-shim necessary rather than optional.
value.it_fired_late: Its charter says it fires at /intent, at the WHAT step. It fired at the cast instead. It would have produced the same split earlier and more cheaply — a point against the operator, not against the probe.
value.its_own_tell_confirmed_verbatim: The probe warns that tool-shaped types are 'born from ARTIFACTS THAT ARE ALREADY BEING PRODUCED rather than from a stated need — the members precede the intention.' Thirteen charters wrote 'device' into the node_class field before anyone ruled it a class, and node_classes/ registers it by nobody. The members preceded the intention by 13 — the same accretion signature as `session`, the case that bore the probe.
value.probe: questions/tool-shaped-or-domain-shaped.json — the corpus's first DISCOVERED probe (2026-07-22), CANDIDATE with ZERO firings until this one.
value.result: It SPLIT the type rather than passing or failing it. The domain concept 'device' is DOMAIN-shaped: imagine BaseDevice gone and Calibre is still a device — a member with zero tool footprint. The current field value 'device' is TOOL-shaped: membership is decided by what inherits BaseDevice, and the measurement says the tool has manufactured SIX members the domain does not have (9 importers vs 3 shims). The improvised sub-kinds are neither — author-shaped, with no tool behavior to imagine away.
value.why_it_was_fired: It is direct prior art for this ticket and it had never run. Explaining an unfired probe's absence is not a diagnostic; calling it is.
